key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal cycling.
engineering_relevance: Engineering adhesion at transparent-conductive-oxide/SAM interfaces offers a route to reduce thermo-mechanical failure in high-efficiency perovskite photovoltaics.
method: Identify stress-accumulation-driven adhesion failure at buried self-assembled monolayer (SAM) interfaces.
Apply a homometallic halide pretreatment to increase surface hydroxyl species and guide ordered SAM assembly.
Strengthen anchoring through metal–oxygen coordination supported by chloride-induced hydrogen bonding.
evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85 °C under ISOS-T-3.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish large-area manufacturing compatibility or long-term outdoor durability beyond the reported thermal-cycling test.
paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
